_README: Structured data for the NOVRA Intelligence site. Three graphs: WebSite, Person, Article.
NO Organization node is emitted, and none may be added until a legal entity
exists and its exact registered name is supplied. NOVRA Intelligence is currently a
masthead — a publication name — not a company. Emitting Organization schema
would assert to search engines that a legal organization exists, which would
be a false machine-readable claim and is explicitly out of scope.
WebSite.name carries the masthead. Person carries the real author. Article
author points at the Person, never at the masthead. That is what lets the
brand front the site while the authority accrues to a real, named human.
Every PLACEHOLDER is unverified and must be filled from fact or deleted.
A deleted field costs nothing. A false one is the whole liability.

website.name: NOVRA Intelligence
website.description: Research and perspectives on artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, blockchain infrastructure, financial technology, and emerging digital systems.

_publisher_note: publisher points at the Person, not an Organization. This is accurate: the
publication is currently published by an individual. schema.org permits a
Person as publisher and it is the honest mapping of the real arrangement.
_person_notes: jobTitle omitted deliberately — not verified. Add only if true and current.
worksFor omitted deliberately. It would require an Organization node, and
BUILDFLOW_PUBLIC_DISCLOSURE=false rules out the one that exists.
alumniOf, award, hasCredential all omitted: nothing verified.
sameAs must list only profiles that resolve and that the subject controls.
A dead or unowned sameAs weakens entity association rather than helping it.
_copy_rules: First person singular throughout. No 'we', 'our team', 'our research'.
Those imply staff who do not exist, which is the same false claim as
Organization schema, just in prose where it is harder to audit.
No counters for papers, projects, systems, clients or years.
The word 'Research' as a section label is fine; 'Research Papers: 87' is not.
